meta.title: Iceland: 7 days, South Coast & Snæfellsnes
meta.room_config: 1 double + 1 single/twin (check for triple/family rooms — often cheaper than two rooms)
meta.fx_note: Approximate mid-2026 rates used for conversions: 1 EUR ≈ 145 ISK, 1 USD ≈ 138 ISK. Re-check before publishing.
meta.purpose: Shareable trip plan for review by two travel companions
meta.schema_notes: Two plan variants (A and B) are peers, not primary/fallback — the site must present them equally with a toggle. Each day has an ordered `stops` array; `drive_to_next_min` and `drive_to_next_km` describe the leg FROM this stop TO the next. `route_waypoints` are for drawing approximate polylines and are NOT the stop list. Times are local (Iceland is GMT year-round, no DST).

daylight.note: Iceland observes GMT year-round. Times below are Reykjavík; Vík is within ~10 minutes. Confirm exact minutes on timeanddate.com for actual travel dates.
daylight.usable_light_window: Approximately 06:50 to 19:30 including twilight, early in the month
daylight.design_hint: The daylight bar visual should span 06:00–21:00 and shade the pre-sunrise and post-sunset portions differently, with each day's stops plotted inside it. This is the element that answers 'will we be rushed?'

locations._comment: Coordinates marked verified came from Google Places lookups. Those marked approximate are good to ~200m and fine for map pins, but should not be used for turn-by-turn navigation.

top_attractions.editorial_note: Several stops on this route that miss a national top 20 are still excellent in person — Fjaðrárgljúfur, Kvernufoss, Djúpalónssandur, Reykjadalur. Rankings favour the famous and the photogenic; the south coast has a deep bench.

practical.daily_checks: Wind is the real disruptor, not cold. Anything over 15 m/s makes waterfall stops miserable and can tear a car door off its hinges — always hold doors when opening.
practical.fuel_cards: Icelandic self-service pumps need a 4-digit PIN on a foreign chip card. Set this up before you fly. Choose a fixed amount rather than 'fill up' to avoid a large pre-authorisation hold.

closed_in_october.note: Highland F-road, shut by late September
Highland F-road, shut by late September
Usually not open until mid-November. Katla is the alternative

practical.volcanic_status: The Reykjanes peninsula has erupted repeatedly since 2023–24 near Sundhnúkur/Grindavík. Grindavík town remains largely restricted; the Blue Lagoon is open as of mid-2026. Conditions change fast — check almannavarnir.is and vedur.is on the day.
practical.northern_lights: Genuinely possible from Day 2 onward. Check the aurora forecast on vedur.is each evening (combined cloud cover + Kp). Get clear of town lights. Best bases: Hvolsvöllur, Hof, Grundarfjörður.
practical.coffee_reality: Outside Reykjavík and the Golden Circle, cafés are sparse and many rural ones cut hours in October. Reliable sit-down stops: Geysir, Skógafoss, Vík, Arnarstapi, Hraunfossar. Everywhere else it's an N1 petrol station — which is fine, but not a lingering experience.
practical.fuel_stops: Fill up at Vík and at Kirkjubæjarklaustur or Höfn. Do not assume you'll find a station further east.

site_build_notes.map_library: Leaflet 1.9.4 from cdnjs. Dark tiles suit the palette (CartoDB dark_all). Attribution is required for both Leaflet and the tile provider.
site_build_notes.signature_element: The daylight bar — each day's stops plotted against actual October sunrise/sunset. This answers the trip's central question ('will we be rushed?') better than any number.
site_build_notes.tone: This is a document three friends will argue over. Be factual, surface trade-offs rather than hiding them, and never oversell a plan.
site_build_notes.accessibility_floor: Responsive to mobile, visible keyboard focus, respects prefers-reduced-motion.
